en: To the Honored Ones throughout all the worlds of the ten directions, And to the Lions among Men who roam through the three periods of time—
Since my body, speech, and mind are fully pure, I now prostrate myself everywhere.
By the power of all vows and the conduct of Samantabhadra, All supreme forms appear before me;
bowing down, my body becomes equal in measure to the dust motes of all buddha-fields.
With a devout heart, I prostrate to the Great Sage, And to the multitude of Buddhas upon every single atom, Each of whom is surrounded by the sons of the Buddha.
These realms of phenomena are all infinite; one should resolve that the Tathāgatas pervade them all.

These oceans of merit are difficult to exhaust, for they are boundless through the branching streams of words that expound the virtues of all Buddhas. Therefore, I shall praise all these virtuous aspirations.
With the most excellent and wondrous flowers and flower garlands, With the most excellent and wondrous lamps and incense burners,
With music, ointments, and precious parasols, And with reverent offerings to all Buddhas—
Excellent garments and fragrant perfumes, Powdered incense piled as high as Mount Sumeru.
With all supreme and wondrous ornaments, I reverently make offerings;
With deep faith in the power of Samantabhadra’s vows and conduct, I perform such unsurpassed and vast acts of giving,
All of which I offer to the Buddhas throughout the ten directions.
With greed, hatred, and delusion as their cause, whatever unwholesome deeds I have committed through the actions of body,
speech, and mind— I now confess them all before the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas of the ten directions, the Pratyekabuddhas, and those in training and beyond training.
And the various merits of all sentient beings— may I rejoice in them all.
To those who act as lamps throughout the realms of the ten directions,
and to such great guides as the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas who have realized non-attachment, I pray that they turn the unsurpassed wheel.
To those Buddhas who wish to enter parinirvāṇa, for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, I join my palms and kneel to entreat them:
may they remain for as many eons as there are atoms in the buddha-fields;
I prostrate, make offerings, and confess my misdeeds; I rejoice in merit, arouse the aspiration for awakening, and offer exhortations.
Whatever small roots of virtue I have accumulated, I dedicate them all toward great enlightenment;
I make offerings to all the Sugatas of the past and ten directions who dwell in the world,
and I cause all the Sugatas of the future to swiftly fulfill their vows and realize enlightenment.
Throughout all the lands of the ten directions, may they all attain vast purity;
may the Honored Ones of Equal Enlightenment beneath the Bodhisattva trees, along with all their spiritual heirs, fulfill their vows;
and may all sentient beings throughout the ten directions obtain untainted, eternal peace and happiness.
May the meaning of all dharmas for all sentient beings be realized; may whatever they hope for be fulfilled according to their wishes as they attain bodhi.
May I practice all the various deeds [of a bodhisattva]; may I be born into the six realms of existence with the wisdom of past lives.
Whenever I receive a body within a world, may the fruit of my renunciation always be achieved.
Following and training in all that is most supreme, may the practices of Samantabhadra be brought to fulfillment;
may my stainless and pure ethical discipline (*śīla*) and so forth remain forever without deficiency or blemish.
May devas, nāgas, yakṣas, kumbhāṇḍas, humans, and all other beings raise their voices [in praise].
According to each and every voice that exists, I shall preach the Dharma for them;
may they become well-disciplined and diligently cultivate the ten perfections.
May they never forget the bodhicitta, and may all those evils that form obstacles be completely extinguished.
Through karma, afflictions, and the various paths of Māra, they move through the world yet attain liberation;
unstained by the world like a lotus in water, they traverse the sky without obstruction like the sun and moon.
Within all the lands of the ten directions, the manifold sufferings of the evil realms are entirely eliminated.
May I bring sentient beings to the state of peace and happiness; Benefiting all practices, may I aid the multitude of beings and enable them to fulfill the conduct of Bodhi.
In accordance with sentient beings, may I turn toward those practices and reveal the conduct of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva;
Throughout all kalpas until the end of the future, may I practice this conduct.
Whoever is able to practice together with me, may they always follow my person;
In their physical, verbal, and mental actions, may they act as one with me.
Those virtuous friends who wish to benefit me, may they expound and manifest all the practices of Samantabhadra.
May I always encounter them in this way; may I never oppose their intentions.
Surrounded by the sons of the Buddha, may I always behold the Great Honored Teacher in person and perform vast offerings within his presence, without weariness throughout all future kalpas.
Constantly upholding the most wondrous Dharma of all Buddhas,
may I universally demonstrate the conduct of Bodhisattvas to purify the practices of Samantabhadra. Throughout future kalpas,
while I wander through the cycle of existence within the three realms, may I realize inexhaustible merit and wisdom.
Concentration, wisdom, skillful means, and liberation—may I fulfill all vows to become an inexhaustible treasury.
Upon every single atom, there are atom-like lands; within each land dwell immeasurable Buddhas, the Honored Ones at their centers, surrounded by their sons.
I gaze up with reverence upon the practices of these Bodhisattvas.
Thus, throughout boundless realms and directions, upon a single hair-tip,
they carry the Buddhas of the three periods of time and their lands, as vast as the ocean; their practices are as numerous as the ocean,
and for many kalpas they speak with a single voice, like the branches of a great sea— these are all the pure voices of the Buddhas.
I shall expound the teachings according to the inclinations of the assembly;
may I always follow the path of the Buddhas’ teachings and roam among the most supreme ones of the three times.
When the unsurpassed wheel of Dharma is turned, may I, through the power of wisdom, cause others to skillfully enter those inexhaustible instructions of all the Buddhas as described above.
All the many kalpas of the future, I shall realize them in a single instant;
throughout these kalpas spanning the three periods of time, I shall traverse them within a fraction of an instant.
O Lion among Men, I shall gaze upon you for all eternity in that very instant.
Constantly, within the supreme realm of all Buddhas, that which is realized through the power of liberation like an illusion—
the adornments of the lands and multitudes throughout the three times— I dedicate them all to be established upon a single atom.
May such infinite directions likewise be universally adorned with Buddha-fields.
May all those who shall realize the truths of future worlds— those who realize equal enlightenment,
turn the wheel of Dharma, demonstrate entry into nirvana, and realize the limit of reality— I vow to practice before all these Buddhas,
so that their various spiritual powers may swiftly go everywhere, and through the power of the Mahayana, they may proceed to the universal gate.
By the power of universal merit through the practice of deeds, by the power of great compassion that is all-pervading and complete,
by the power of all virtues and all blessings, by the power of great wisdom free from attachment,
by the power of wisdom, skillful means, and meditative concentration, may the power of correctly practicing for enlightenment be attained.
By the power of always purifying all karmic actions, And by the power of forever eliminating all afflictions;
May the powers of all Māras be rendered powerless, And the power of Samantabhadra’s conduct be perfected.
May all world-systems, vast as oceans, be purified, And may the ocean-like multitudes of sentient beings be liberated.
May all phenomena, like the ocean, be clearly perceived; May wisdom, like the ocean, be excellently realized;
May practices, like the ocean, be purified; May vows, like the ocean, be brought to fulfillment;
May the Buddhas, like the ocean, be honored with offerings; And throughout oceans of kalpas, may practice continue without weariness.

Wandering through the three periods of time, the most supreme among honored ones, Having attained perfect enlightenment through the manifold practices and vows of Bodhicitta, such as the conduct of Samantabhadra, In this way, I shall bring them all to fulfillment;
among the sons of the Buddhas, I shall be the most honored. For this reason, I am named Samantabhadra.
Because I practice together with this great wisdom, I dedicate all such virtues toward the utter purity of the actions of body,
speech, and mind. Just as Samantabhadra purifies the lands he traverses and performs such perfect dedications, may I likewise follow his example in these practices.
I shall practice the supreme and universal conduct of Samantabhadra;
I shall also fulfill the great vows of Mañjuśrī. Throughout all future kalpas, may I never grow weary or exhausted;
May these practices of the Bodhisattva be brought to complete perfection, And may such deeds as these be immeasurable, And likewise, may all merits be immeasurable.
Abiding in such immeasurable practices, may I know all transformations;
as long as the limits of space endure, so too shall sentient beings be inexhaustible.
As long as the limits of karma and afflictions endure, the extent of my vows shall likewise remain.
All the infinite lands of the ten directions, adorned with various jewels,
And the supreme bliss of humans and great beings— Were one to offer these for as many eons as there are motes of dust in those lands,
Would it be equal to hearing this Sūtra of Dedication, Which accords with and inspires deep faith in Great Bodhi?
If one gives rise to even a single faith in this, One immediately accomplishes a most supreme mass of merit.
If a person makes these vows of Samantabhadra, They will thereby remain far removed from all evil realms.
Furthermore, by abandoning all evil companions, Such a person will swiftly behold Amitābha.
All these shall attain the most supreme longevity; welcome to this human life of long duration!
Just as the Great Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, all shall be able to achieve swift accomplishment before long.
Who, through the power of ignorance, has committed the five crimes of immediate retribution and other such manifold sins?
If that person recites this *Samantabhadra-praṇidhāna*, they shall swiftly attain the ultimate limit of exhaustion at that very moment;
in all physical forms and wisdom, as well as in lineage and physical presence, they shall be perfectly complete.
No demons or non-Buddhists shall be able to subdue them, and throughout the three realms, they shall be universally honored for their Way.
For the sake of benefiting all sentient beings, may you swiftly dwell beneath the Bodhi tree, attain perfect enlightenment, and turn the wheel of Dharma; may you subdue all hosts of Māra.
For those who uphold, recite, read, and explain such vows of conduct as these of Samantabhadra—
The retribution of this is known only by the Buddha; do not give rise to doubt regarding unsurpassed bodhi.
Just as Mañjuśrī possesses majestic power, wisdom, and virtue, so too does Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
Following their example, I shall train and act just as they do; all such virtues I dedicate entirely.
Whatever roots of goodness I have thus dedicated toward the praise of those most supreme ones who range through the three times,
I dedicate them for the practice of the conduct of Samantabhadra.
When my life comes to its end, may all obscurations be utterly cleared away.
Having personally beheld Amitābha with my own eyes, And having arrived within that land of Ultimate Bliss,
May these vows as they are thus made Be realized in their entirety before me;
May all these be perfectly fulfilled, Benefiting all sentient beings throughout the worlds until the end of time.

In the most beautiful buddha-field of Sukhāvatī, May I be born upon a sublime lotus flower And stand directly before the World-Honored One Amitābha; May I receive the prediction of enlightenment here,
And having received this most supreme prediction, May I manifest hundreds of billions of emanations.
May they, through the power of their generosity, bring benefit to all sentient beings throughout the ten directions.
—From the *Sūtra of the Vows and Practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva* (Bhadracarī-praṇidhāna-rāja-sūtra).
